title: Spanning Trees of K_n
prompt: By Cayley's formula, how many labelled spanning trees does K_10 have?
recap:
Cayley's formula: K_n has exactly n^(n-2) labelled spanning trees — a count that explodes with n.

It follows from the Prüfer code, a bijection between labelled trees on n vertices and length-(n−2) strings over {1,…,n}; there are n^(n−2) of them.

Example — K₄ has 4² = 16 spanning trees.

Reference: Aigner & Ziegler, Proofs from THE BOOK (Cayley's formula).
